articles.title: BlackRock says markets overprice Fed hikes, sees two not three as energy shock fades
articles.expand: BlackRock's view runs against Monday's hawkish Fed commentary and against market pricing, so the October PCE data becomes a key test. A softer services reading would back BlackRock and could pull Fed pricing toward two hikes, supporting short-dated Treasuries and easing some pressure on the US dollar. For oil, BlackRock's case depends on the recent sharp fall in crude and fuel prices holding. A renewed rise in energy costs would undercut its view and strengthen the case for more Fed tightening. articles.title: Fed's Williams won't rule out back-to-back rate hikes as data drives the path
articles.expand: The openness to consecutive hikes adds upside risk to Fed pricing beyond December, with traders more likely to build in a follow-up move in early 2027. That should keep short-dated Treasury yields supported and give the US dollar a firmer floor, especially against currencies whose central banks are moving toward cuts. For equities, Williams set a high bar for market weakness to change his view, which limits hopes that renewed tech volatility would slow the Fed. Energy remains central to his inflation outlook, so any rise in oil prices would add weight to the case for a faster pace of hikes. --...

articles.title: ANZ pulls first RBA rate cut forward to June 2027, sees three cuts by early 2028
articles.expand: The bigger story for currency markets is the policy divergence. The RBA is now widely expected to start easing in mid-2027, while the Fed is still on a hiking path, with a December increase broadly expected. A narrowing rate gap between the two would weigh on the Australian dollar against the US dollar over time. Short-dated Australian rates may see limited reaction, because markets had already priced a June cut as more likely than not after the jobs data. The effect is more likely to show up further out on the curve. Any upside surprise in quarterly inflation would test ANZ's call quickly and...

Fed's Williams pins inflation on unusual factors, sees 2027 bringing it lower
articles.expand: The Q A softens the tone of Williams' prepared remarks without changing their core message, so pricing for a quarter-point hike on December 9 is unlikely to move much. His focus on unusual factors puts energy back at the centre. Brent is still around $92, well above the roughly $72 seen in late February before the US war with Iran began, so oil remains the main factor in how quickly 2027 delivers the lower inflation he expects. A sustained fall in crude would strengthen the case for a shallower hiking path next year, while fresh supply disruption would push the other way. His caution on hiring...

articles.expand: Williams' remarks support pricing for a quarter-point hike in December and further tightening in 2027, which should keep front-end Treasury yields firm and give the US dollar some support. articles.title: USDCAD trades to new 2025 highs and stretches toward the next targets
articles.expand: USDCAD is pushing to its highest level since April 2025 as broad US dollar buying and higher Treasury yields give the pair another lift. The 2-year yield is up 9.36 basis points, while the 10-year yield is up 3.4 basis points. Markets are now pricing in a nearly 100% chance of a Fed rate hike in December. At the end of last week, there was still about a 6% chance the Fed would leave policy unchanged. articles.title: SNB's Martin eyes second-round effects after inflation jumps to 1.5%, hike in view
articles.expand: Martin's focus on second-round effects is a hawkish signal, and it supports pricing for a December SNB hike. A tightening Swiss central bank alongside a hiking Fed changes the usual rate-differential story for the franc. Combined with strong safe-haven demand during the equity rout, that could keep the franc well bid, especially against the euro. That is the very currency risk Martin flagged, so the SNB may stay willing to lean against excessive franc strength even as it tightens. articles.title: Australia flash PMI sinks to 46.1 as private sector shrinks at fastest pace in 5 years
articles.expand: A drop this deep, alongside the first easing in input cost inflation for months, weakens the case for further Australian monetary tightening. That leaves the Australian dollar exposed if rate markets start pricing a gentler path. The sharp fall in new export orders also points to softening external demand, at a time when global equities are already under heavy pressure. Prices are still running above their long-run averages, though, so policymakers are unlikely to move quickly to declare inflation beaten. Any boost may be short-lived, though, with global risk appetite under heavy pressure after last week's Wall Street rout. A high-beta currency like the kiwi tends to follow broader sentiment in that kind of market.
